thyroxine (T4) tetraiodothyronine (thyroxine) long-
acting hormone released by the thyroid gland that 
can be converted to T3 
triiodothyronine (T3) hormone released by the 
thyroid gland to help regulate processes including 
metabolism, weight, and energy levels 
type 1 diabetes insulin-dependent diabetes; 
develops when insulin producing cells (beta cells) 
are destroyed in the pancreas, resulting in low to 
non-existent levels of insulin 
type 2 diabetes noninsulin-dependent diabetes; 
results from insulin resistance that develops 
gradually from obesity and aging 
Review Questions 
1 . How does protein intake contribute to growth and development during childhood? 
a. Maintains digestive function 
b. Influences nutrient absorption 
c. Plays an anabolic role similar to that of growth hormone 
d. Mediates levels of growth hormone 
2 . Which of the following foods supplies micronutrients that decrease inflammation? 
a. Kale 
b. Sourdough bread 
c. Beef 
d. White rice 
3 . Medications given to older adults to stimulate appetite target which hormone? 
a. Ghrelin 
b. Thyroid-stimulating hormone 
c. Insulin 
d. Cholecystokinin 
4 . Which of the following is a good food choice for a client with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis who needs to consume 
iodine-rich foods? 
a. Leafy green vegetables 
b. Fish 
c. Citrus fruits 
d. Whole grains
